Q: Is there anyway to extract live data from listed products (ei 1oz gold bar) for apps script? A:

You should analyse the page source code. Only if the data is included in it you might use Apps Script to retrieve it. If the data that you want to scrape is added dynamically then Apps Script is not the right tool for this task.

Q: Getting a ConnectionString empty error in a webapi project with .net 10 A:

The issue is that you are using the value of the "DefaultConnection" connection string that you retrieved first as a key for a second lookup in the same connection strings config section.

var connString = configuration.GetConnectionString("DefaultConnection");

builder.Services.AddDbContext<POA_CSMContext>(options => options.UseSqlServer(
   configuration.GetConnectionString(connString))); // <-- second lookup with 
                                                    // the value of the DefaultConnection as the key

Q: Spring MVC REST API - one endpoint for many roles or separate endpoints? A:

Should I then create two separate routes

From a REST perspective: It's not necessary to use different routes.

Both REST generally and HTTP specifically give you the freedom to choose when to reply 403 Forbidden rather than 200 Success. So if you want to reject a request from Pat because of instructions in the patch document provided, you're allowed to do that.

In other words, nothing in the HTTP specification requires that you limit yourself to coarse-grained access controls.

But you certainly can use separate resources, which you might prefer because (a) you are happier with the information in the access logs, (b) you are happier with the api documentation, (c) your most important customer wants it that way (d) you just feel like it.

Note that both of those are "could". "Should" is a more complicated question, and getting to the best answer requires understanding your context and the trade offs involved.

(For instance, you might choose one variant because Spring makes implementing that variant much easier than the other. Or you might instead decide that Spring's opinion is less important than realizing some other benefit.)

My strongest suggestion is to be certain that you have a Decision Record describing the tradeoffs as you understand them and why you made the choice that you did.

Q: Static URL for Google Apps script? A:

From the question

This URL changes with each iteration of the code

This happens when creating a new deployment. You should create a new version instead.

Related standard question: How to Re-publish Web App without changing URL

Q: Build a class diagram with a user multirole A:

The usual way

As the quote goes:

Any problem in computer science can be solved with another layer of indirection.

You are answering 'What is a use-case for polymorphism in software design?' with a question.

See S.O.L.I.D. principles for more on best-practices beyond that.

In summation: abstract the common aspects of both into a third class (perhaps even and abstract class ... or interface/protocol/etc. depending on implementing language), E.g. agent. Now sub-class agent (or otherwise depending on implementing language again) for both listener & musician (depending on limits of multiple inheritance, you may need another abstract object)

Example with Python-style multiple inheritance:

     agent (class)
     /   \
    /     \
   /       \
  r         \
  |          \
  |           \
  |            \
  |             \
  |              \
listener (class)  \ 
   \            musician (class)
    \            /
     \          /
      \        /
       \      /
        \    /
         \  /
        MultiAgent (class)

     agent (optional common scope)
     /    \
    /      \
   /        \
  r          \
  |           \
  |            \

  |                      \

agent.listener (interface) \ 
  | \                      agent.musician (interface)
  |  \                    /    |
  |   \                  /     |
  |    \                /      |
  |     \              /     agent.justmusician (class)
  |      \            /
  |       \          /
  |        \        /
  |         \      /
  |          \    /
  |           \  /
  |       agent.both (class)
  |
 agent.justlistener (class)

Note: protocols are similar to interfaces in the diagram scope.

Edge-case where there is no functional difference:

In the case where there is no functional difference between the three, just keep it simple and make the agent's role a variable (e.g. just another data field) no relation nor class needed.

    agent (class)
      * protected id,
      * public role,
      * etc.
